newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher Canada plans Blandin upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Canada plans Blandin upgrade.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd said Tuesday it plans a US$32 million upgrade of a paper machine at its Blandin unit in Minnesota that will increase output of ultra-lightweight catalogue paper by 42,000 tons a year.
The project is expected to be completed in early 1998.

Fletcher Canada is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd. In the upgrade, the number six paper machine at Blandin will have its existing headbox and twin-wire former replaced by state-of-the-art gap-former technology.

Fletcher said the machine is already one of North America's largest and fastest lightweight coated machines. It was installed in 1989. In recent years, gap-former technology has become the new lightweight paper forming standard, resulting in a more uniform sheet that performs better on modern high-speed printing presses.
Blandin currently has capacity for 475,000 tons of lightweight coated paper a year.
